title: Man dies in RCMP custody: Police arrested 30-year-old for assault, being drunk
article: Creston Mayor Joe Snopek is in mourning today over the death of his 30-year-old nephew in police custody in Cranbrook on New Year's Day.
Ryan Glen Snopek stopped breathing in the Cranbrook RCMP cells and died.
"He was my brother's son," Snopek said yesterday. "He was here on Christmas Day," which is the last time Snopek saw his nephew.

Snopek said his brother Rudy and Rudy's wife, Glenda, drove to Creston on Sunday from their home in Whitecourt, Alta., 170 kilometres northwest of Edmonton, after learning of their son's death. The parents would not comment.
Snopek said the RCMP called him about the death and he had detailed discussions about it but would not reveal what he was told.

RCMP said they arrested Snopek, who lived in Cranbrook, for assault, mischief and for being drunk in a public place after being called to a disturbance at a Cranbrook home at 9 p.m. on New Year's Eve.
"Upon arrival, police discovered Ryan Glen Snopek apparently passed out on the steps of the residence," Cranbrook Cpl. Chris Faulkner said in a statement.
Police at the scene were told that Snopek had been taken out of the home because he had been causing a disturbance.
"Snopek was examined by the Cranbrook first responders \[fire department\] and the B.C. Ambulance service personnel, then arrested by police," Faulkner said.
Police then took Snopek to the cells. At 9:53 a.m. on New Year's Day, a guard noticed that "Snopek was having difficulty breathing and alerted the police members on duty," said Faulkner.
"Three members attended immediately and noted that Snopek was not breathing," he said. "They initiated CPR and continued until emergency services personnel took over."
Snopek was taken to Cranbrook Regional Hospital and pronounced dead at 1:36 p.m.
RCMP said they do not know the cause of death and an autopsy will be done.
RCMP's major crime unit from Kelowna will investigate. It is standard procedure for the major crime section to investigate all deaths in police custody.
Cranbrook RCMP did not return phone calls to explain why Snopek was not sent to hospital to be checked, instead of jail, when he was found passed out prior to being arrested.
